Theme

Latin word

significō

significō, significāre, significāvī, significātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive

give to understand, intimate, hint; indicate, show, make known; mean, signify (of a word or a sign)

In this lexicon

  • imply

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.3.213: hoc mihi significāsse et annuisse vīsus est (Lewis & Short)

  • indicate

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.18.1: significābant enim tē istam mīlitiam jam firmō animō ferre; Traupman 247, 332: significāre, indicate; Traupman 332

  • mean

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Tusc. 1.88: carēre igitur hoc significat: egēre eō quod habēre velīs; Traupman 30; Traupman 247

Examples

  • hoc mihi significāsse et annuisse vīsus est

    he seemed to hint this to me and nodCic. Verr. 2.3.213 (Lewis & Short)

    if this statement is not true, it follows that it is falseCic. Fat. 28 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for imply

  • significābant enim tē istam mīlitiam jam firmō animō ferre et esse fortem virum et cōnstantem

    for they showed that you are now bearing your military service with a steady mind, and are a brave and steadfast manCic. Fam. 7.18.1
